messages:
eli: Heads-up — after last night's CUDA driver rollforward we saw kernel-selection churn on H100 pools causing 99th p90 spikes for medium sequences (256-1024). Noticing KV-prefetch rate jumps too.
sanju: Saw that on metrics dashboard. Throughput dipped ~7% on the affected dedicated fleet, latency up ~120ms at tail.
priya: Is this the autotuner changing from the vectorized attention kernels back to fallback slotted kernels? Sequence-length classifier is oscillating?
maria: Quick snapshot from a few canaries — autotune history shows rapid kernel flips for seq=512: v1->v3->v1 within minutes. Hitrate for cached KV also dropped when path flipped.
ops-bot: Incident detected: kernel_selection_entropy > threshold on pool:dedicated-h100-1, alert_id: A-9281
eli: Posting a short grep of the runtime logs from last deploy window:
```
[2026-03-17T02:14:05Z] kernel_picker: seq_len=512 chosen=attn_vec_v1 score=0.32
[2026-03-17T02:14:30Z] kernel_picker: seq_len=512 chosen=attn_slotted score=0.35
[2026-03-17T02:15:12Z] autotuner: rollback_candidate=attn_vec_v1 reason=throughput_regression
[2026-03-17T02:16:03Z] kernel_picker: seq_len=512 chosen=attn_vec_v1 score=0.33
[2026-03-17T02:16:40Z] kernel_picker: seq_len=512 chosen=attn_slotted score=0.36
```
eli: So it's not a single bad pick — autotuner keeps flipping and that disrupts KV-prefetch alignment which raises tail latency.
priya: Could be driver-level timing changes altering kernel runtime microbenchmarks used by the autotuner scoring fn. We've seen microsecond shifts break heuristics before.
sanju: Agree. We should either (A) pin kernel selection to the last-known-good mapping for the fleet, or (B) disable autotune and force stable heuristic until we fully repro.
maria: For immediate mitigation I propose we set deterministic kernel selection for seq ranges: 0-128 -> attn_vec, 129-768 -> attn_vec_v1 (pin), >768 -> attn_slotted. That reduces flips and keeps KV-prefetch consistent.
jen: +1. Also suggest we throttle autotune sampling rate — drop it to 1% of traffic so it can still gather stats without causing churn.
priya: Steps to implement rollback/mitigation:
1) Canary push deterministic map to canary fleet (dedicated-h100-canary) with sampling off.
2) Monitor tail latency + KV-prefetch hitrate for 30m.
3) If stable, roll to remaining pools and reduce autotune to passive mode.
4) Re-run autotune microbenchmarks in CI using the upgraded driver to recalibrate scoring.
eli: Commands I'll run for quick toggles (ops runbook):
```
# pin kernel map for pool
redwoodctl runtime set --pool dedicated-h100-1 --kernels-map '{"0-128":"attn_vec","129-768":"attn_vec_v1","769-4096":"attn_slotted"}'
# pause autotuner
redwoodctl runtime set --autotuner.enabled false --pool dedicated-h100-1
# set sampling
redwoodctl runtime set --autotuner.sample_rate 0.01 --pool dedicated-h100-canary
```
sanju: Can you add a quick smoke script to validate KV-prefetch alignment? We need to ensure cached KV nodes are used after pinning (not just kernel selection metrics).
priya: I'll spin up a local harness that replays typical seq-length distribution and checks KV hit rate and per-token latency. Attaching expected assertions:
- KV hitrate >= 98% after warmup
- p95 latency within 15% of baseline
- kernel selection flips <= 1 per hour
maria: If canary shows improvement, we should avoid a full driver rollback now — rollback is disruptive. Try pinned kernels + autotune passive first.
eli: If pinned map fails to stabilize within 60m, plan B is to roll the driver back on the affected node image and force the fleet to use the last driver version that had low entropy.
jen: Note: compliance/infra will need a changelog entry for any kernel-map pin or driver rollback. Ops will create a ticket.
ops-bot: Created ticket: INF-4472 - Investigate kernel pick entropy post-driver-upgrade; assignees: priya, sanju, eli
sanju: I'll run the canary deploy now and watch metrics. ping me in this thread if you see anything odd. :eyes:
eli: Thanks — I'll coordinate the rollout and keep updates here. Let's keep autotuner off for the main fleet until next scheduled recalibration.
maria: Also recommend capturing performance counters (smem, l2, tensor core utilization) during the canary to feed into the autotuner re-tune job.
priya: On it, I'll attach a small perf-collector script to the canary agents.
jen: After stabilization we should add a guard to the autotuner: require 1h stable p95 improvement before any automated commit.
eli: Agreed. Adding that to the autotune safeties backlog item.
sanju: Canary deployed -> monitoring. Will report back at +15m, +30m.
eli: update after 15m: KV hitrate up ~3% and tail latency dropping ~80ms on canary. Looks promising.
maria: Good sign. Hold on full roll until 30m check.
eli: update after 30m: stable. proceeding with staged rollout and leaving autotune sample at 1% for calibration. Will keep thread open for any regressions.
